query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Interstitial carbon doping at ~0.5 at% in MnNiSi-based alloys improves mechanical fracture toughness and ductility by segregating to grain boundaries and inhibiting crack propagation, while retaining at least 90% of the baseline magnetocaloric entropy change under a 5 T field.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline MnNiSi alloy synthesized by arc-melting and homogenized at 1173 K for 48 h (undoped baseline).
generation.intervention: Add 0.5 at% C via mechanical alloying followed by annealing at 973 K for 12 h to achieve interstitial carbon incorporation.
generation.conditions: Testing at ambient temperature (300 K), magnetic field sweep ΔH = 0→5 T; microstructure fixed by the specified annealing.
generation.structural_mediator: Interstitial C atoms segregate to grain boundaries, increasing grain‐boundary cohesion and impeding crack‐tip propagation.
generation.mechanism: Carbon at grain boundaries raises boundary‐cohesion energy and dislocation‐emission resistance near boundaries, boosting fracture toughness without significantly straining the lattice parameters responsible for the magnetostructural transition.
generation.predicted_outcome: Fracture toughness K_IC increases by ≥30% (from ~2.0 to ≥2.6 MPa·m^0.5), flexural failure strain increases by ≥25% (from ~1.6% to ≥2.0%), and peak |ΔS_M| under ΔH=5 T remains ≥90% of the undoped value (from ~35 to ≥31 J·kg^−1·K^−1).
generation.baseline: Undoped MnNiSi: K_IC ≈2.0 MPa·m^0.5, failure strain ≈1.6%, peak |ΔS_M|(5 T,300 K) ≈35 J·kg^−1·K^−1.
generation.boundary: Holds for C content between 0.3–0.7 at% and annealing at 973 K/12 h; outside this range, segregation behavior and magnetic transition may change.
generation.uncertainty: Precise C solubility and distribution can vary with processing, affecting the magnitude of mechanical gains and the exact retention of magnetocaloric performance.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of MnNiSi samples (with and without 0.5 at% C) under identical melting and annealing protocols. Measure fracture toughness by single‐edge notched bending and flexural failure strain, and determine peak |ΔS_M| under ΔH=0→5 T at 300 K.
measurements: Peak magnetic entropy change |ΔS_M| under ΔH=5 T
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the C-doped alloy shows <15% improvement in K_IC relative to undoped or retains <90% of the baseline |ΔS_M| under a 5 T field.
